proposals.hole: A tracker-born item can be attested against an arbitrary file at the required path rather than a fresh rendering of its canonical tracker data. The record, marker, and claim can all agree on those unrelated bytes while the item's actual criteria remain unattacked.
proposals.proposed_ac: For a tracker-born item, attestation is refused unless `.work/attacks/<item-id>.md` is byte-equal to a fresh `work acceptance render <item-id>` result, and no marker is written on mismatch.

red_test_sketch.expect: Attestation is refused naming the rendering mismatch, and the item receives no marker.

proposals.hole: The stale-facade check covers the attack path, panel, and poster but not `work claim` itself. An older facade without the claim gate can claim an empty or unattacked item.
proposals.proposed_ac: Every supported claim path refuses before mutation when the `work` binary on PATH predates the version that ships the criteria and attestation gate, naming the required version.

red_test_sketch.expect: The claim is refused with the required facade version, and the item remains open.

red_test_sketch.when: An agent invokes the supported claim workflow.

proposals.hole: The criteria do not require the claim transition and its rendering validation to be atomic. A claim can validate a marker, race with a completed criteria amendment, and still transition the now-stale item to in progress.
proposals.proposed_ac: A claim may transition an item to in progress only if the acceptance data used to select and hash the attackable document remains unchanged through the state transition.

red_test_sketch.expect: The claim is refused as stale and the item remains open.
red_test_sketch.given: An open, validly attested tracker-born item with a claim paused after reading its marker but before committing the state transition.
red_test_sketch.when: A criteria amendment completes and then the paused claim resumes.

proposals.hole: A1 requires tracker-born description edits to invalidate an attestation but never pins the inverse. An implementation can invalidate spec-born children on description-only edits even though their attackable document is the spec.
proposals.proposed_ac: Editing only the description of a spec-born item leaves its spec-backed attestation valid and does not require another attack.

red_test_sketch.expect: The item claims successfully using the existing marker and unchanged spec record.
red_test_sketch.given: An open, attested spec-born child whose cited spec and criteria field are unchanged.
red_test_sketch.when: Only the child's description is edited and the child is claimed.

proposals.hole: A3 exercises individual example records but does not prove that the gate discovers every record location. A checker hard-coded to one directory can pass the listed cases while silently skipping spec-adjacent or nested records.
proposals.proposed_ac: The whole-repository gate discovers every attack-record file recursively, including records beside specs and records under `.work/attacks/`, and reports every invalid record found in one run.

red_test_sketch.expect: The gate exits nonzero and names both invalid record paths.
red_test_sketch.given: A tree containing one invalid record beside a nested spec and another invalid record under `.work/attacks/`, plus valid records in both locations.
red_test_sketch.when: The whole-repository attack-record gate runs.

proposals.hole: A6 requires historical records to be rerun during registration but does not require the checker to reject later records that omit the behavioural-outcome lens. A newly handcrafted record can close without that lens.
proposals.proposed_ac: The checker refuses every record whose closing round does not contain a completed behavioural-outcome lens result for the closing revision.

red_test_sketch.expect: The checker exits nonzero, names the record, and reports the missing required lens.

proposals.hole: The criteria do not pin the dependency-failure behavior for the new lens. A transport failure can be treated as an empty result and allow the round to close.
proposals.proposed_ac: If the behavioural-outcome lens cannot run or return a valid result, the attack remains open and identifies that lens failure; it is never recorded as an empty successful result.

red_test_sketch.expect: No closed record is produced, and the failure names the unavailable behavioural-outcome lens.
red_test_sketch.given: A criterion set ready for attack and a harness in which the behavioural-outcome lens transport fails.
red_test_sketch.when: The attack round runs.

proposals.hole: The slice calls the behavioural-outcome lens first-ranked, but no criterion checks ordering. It can be registered last while satisfying the findings and closure checks.
proposals.proposed_ac: When an attack round has multiple lenses, the behavioural-outcome lens is dispatched before every other lens.

red_test_sketch.expect: The recorded dispatch sequence starts with the behavioural-outcome lens.
red_test_sketch.given: An attack configuration containing the behavioural-outcome lens and at least two other lenses with observable dispatch events.
red_test_sketch.when: A round is started.

proposals.hole: The standard requires every taxonomy row to be resolved or ruled out with a reason, but A6 checks only the behavioural shape of criteria. A well-formed happy-path criterion with no inverse, boundary, dependency, concurrency, or idempotency analysis can pass.
proposals.proposed_ac: For every criterion, the attack reports each missing applicable edge-case outcome and each taxonomy row ruled out without a reason; the record cannot close until all five rows are resolved or justified.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack returns findings for every unresolved taxonomy row, and the record remains open.

red_test_sketch.when: The criterion set is attacked.

proposals.hole: A4 does not state the taxonomy's empty-rendering rule. The panel or poster can accept an empty file when it is byte-equal to a fresh empty rendering.

proposals.hole: A4 makes the poster fail closed when rendering cannot be obtained but does not impose the same requirement on the panel. The panel can proceed with a hand-typed or stale file after a render failure.
proposals.proposed_ac: For a tracker-backed target, the panel refuses to emit a round when a fresh rendering cannot be obtained, naming the rendering failure and never falling back to the supplied file.

red_test_sketch.expect: Round emission is refused with the render error, and no attacker receives the supplied file.

red_test_sketch.when: The panel attempts to emit the round.

proposals.hole: The decision preserves supplied criteria for targets with no tracker item, but no acceptance criterion protects that behavior. An implementation can reject all such reviews.
proposals.proposed_ac: For a review target with no tracker item, the panel and verdict poster continue to accept and use the supplied criteria file without requiring a facade rendering.

proposals.hole: A5 does not pin the whole-line citation boundary. A parser can treat any line containing an ID as a citation and corrupt ordinary prose that merely mentions an ID.
proposals.proposed_ac: With a named spec, only a line whose entire content matches the shared criterion-ID grammar is resolved as a citation; lines that prefix, suffix, or embed the same ID render as text.

proposals.hole: No acceptance criterion pins the canonical bullet grammar that downstream parsers rely on. A renderer and its immediate consumers can agree on JSON or another private format while passing the byte-equality checks.
proposals.proposed_ac: Every resolved criterion is emitted in the existing Markdown grammar `- **ID** text`, and the output is accepted unchanged by both spec-lint's criterion parser and the verdict poster's criterion parser.

proposals.hole: A9 checks that description changes affect tracker-born attestations but never checks that the description is actually readable in the attack document. A renderer can include only a description hash or hidden token.

proposals.hole: A10 says 'at or past' but does not pin semantic version comparison. Lexical comparison can reject `1.10.0` as older than `1.9.0`, or accept malformed and prerelease versions incorrectly.
proposals.proposed_ac: Facade minimum-version checks use semantic version precedence, accept a stable version equal to or newer than the required release, reject older and prerelease versions when the stable release is required, and refuse unparseable version output by name.

red_test_sketch.when: Each guarded workflow performs its version check.

proposals.hole: A11 checks repeated attestation but does not require the concurrent case stated in the taxonomy. Two racing invocations can append duplicate marker notes.
proposals.proposed_ac: Concurrent attestations of the same item, record, and document produce exactly one marker note and both invocations return the same successful final state.

proposals.hole: A8 requires every listed test to map to a criterion but does not require every assigned criterion to have evidence. A brief can map all tests to one easy criterion and leave the others unsupported.

proposals.hole: The document says every criteria consumer uses the render verb, but the criteria enumerate only the attack path, panel, poster, and briefing behavior. Another deployed consumer can retain an independent acceptance-field parser or copied criteria bytes.
proposals.proposed_ac: An inventory of deployed criteria consumers finds that each tracker-backed consumer obtains its criteria through `work acceptance render`; adding a consumer that parses the acceptance field directly or accepts a retyped tracker-backed copy makes the repository gate fail and names that consumer.

red_test_sketch.expect: The conformance gate fails and identifies the direct parser as bypassing the canonical rendering path.

red_test_sketch.when: The criteria-consumer conformance check runs.

proposals.hole: A claim can validate an attestation and then race with a criteria or description amendment before committing the open-to-in-progress transition, allowing the transition to succeed against stale criteria.
proposals.proposed_ac: A claim racing an amendment is serializable: it either completes before the amendment, or it observes the amended attackable document and refuses the stale attestation; it never enters in_progress with an attestation for an older document.

red_test_sketch.expect: The final state is equivalent to one complete ordering, and no successful claim is bound to the pre-amendment digest when the amendment wins.
red_test_sketch.given: An open tracker-born feat with a valid attestation and a barrier that can pause claim after validation but before the state transition.
red_test_sketch.when: The claim and a criteria or description amendment execute across the barrier.

proposals.hole: The criteria do not cover an item changing between tracker-born and spec-born after an attestation, so an attestation for the old document class might survive the classification boundary.

red_test_sketch.given: An attested item whose criteria make it spec-born, followed by an equivalent item whose amended field makes it tracker-born, and the reverse transition.
red_test_sketch.when: Each amended item is claimed without a new attack and attestation.
red_test_sketch.expect: Both claims are refused, and each becomes claimable only after attacking and attesting the document selected by its new classification.

proposals.hole: Changing the spec named by an item is not listed among attestation-invalidating mutations, even though it changes citation resolution and may change which spec record binds the item.
proposals.proposed_ac: Changing an item's named spec invalidates any prior attestation; subsequent rendering and attestation use only the newly named spec.

red_test_sketch.given: An attested citation-only item whose cited ID exists with different text in two specs.
red_test_sketch.when: The item's named spec changes and the item is claimed without re-attack.
red_test_sketch.expect: The render uses the new spec's text and the claim refuses the old attestation until the new attackable document is attacked and attested.

proposals.hole: Round emission and verdict posting can compare a criteria file with a fresh render and then race with an amendment before performing the external emission or post.
proposals.proposed_ac: Round emission and verdict posting are serializable with criteria amendments: neither emits or posts criteria after the item has changed from the rendering that was validated.

red_test_sketch.expect: The side effect is refused and no round or verdict is emitted with the stale criteria.

proposals.hole: Rendering can race with updates to the description, criteria field, or named spec and produce bytes assembled from more than one item revision.
proposals.proposed_ac: A render concurrent with an item or spec mutation returns one complete revision or refuses; it never combines description or criteria bytes from different revisions.

red_test_sketch.given: An item whose old and new revisions have distinguishable descriptions and criterion text, with reads paused between components.
red_test_sketch.when: Rendering runs concurrently with the revision change.
red_test_sketch.expect: The output equals the complete old render or the complete new render, or the render refuses; no mixed output is returned.

proposals.hole: D2 treats every non-citation line as text while A2 treats whitespace-only criteria as empty, leaving blank lines in mixed fields able to become phantom criteria or change tracker-born versus spec-born classification.
proposals.proposed_ac: Empty and whitespace-only lines are ignored for rendering and for spec-born classification, including leading, trailing, and repeated blank lines around citations or text.

proposals.hole: No criterion defines how a cited spec entry with multiline text is rendered, so continuation lines, nested bullets, or blank paragraphs may be truncated or reinterpreted as additional criteria.

red_test_sketch.expect: All content appears once and in order under that criterion's rendered bullet, with no truncation or extra criterion.

proposals.hole: The criteria do not specify repeated citations to the same valid ID in one acceptance field, so implementations may duplicate, deduplicate, or refuse them inconsistently.
proposals.proposed_ac: When the same valid criterion ID appears more than once in an item's field, rendering follows one explicitly tested rule and remains byte-stable across repeated renders.

red_test_sketch.when: The item is rendered twice.
red_test_sketch.expect: Both renders are byte-equal and apply the specified duplicate-citation behavior consistently without changing field order.

proposals.hole: Resolved criterion text that itself looks like a criterion ID or rendered criterion bullet can be recursively interpreted, creating unintended lookup or duplication.
proposals.proposed_ac: Citation resolution is single-pass: text obtained from a spec entry is rendered literally and is never treated as another citation.

red_test_sketch.expect: The entry's text appears literally once, and no second ID is resolved from that text.

proposals.hole: A5 covers a missing spec but not an unreadable or syntactically invalid spec, allowing dependency failure to be mistaken for an empty or unresolved criterion.

red_test_sketch.given: Two items naming specs that respectively cannot be read and contain invalid criterion syntax.
red_test_sketch.when: Each item is rendered or claimed.
red_test_sketch.expect: Each operation refuses, names the affected path and failure cause, and emits no partial rendering.

proposals.hole: An artifact criterion can name a nonexistent, duplicated, or artifact-only criterion as the behavioural criterion it serves and still appear to satisfy the wording that it names one.

red_test_sketch.when: The behavioural-outcome lens attacks each set.
red_test_sketch.expect: Each set receives a finding identifying the invalid serves reference, and its record cannot close without disposition.

proposals.hole: A8 permits a 'verbatim subset' without requiring that subset to be nonempty or to contain every criterion assigned to the subagent, so a brief can omit the operative criteria while still listing evidence.
proposals.proposed_ac: A subagent brief includes every rendered criterion assigned to that dispatch verbatim; any permitted subset is nonempty and is exactly the explicitly selected scope, with every evidence entry mapped to at least one included criterion.

red_test_sketch.given: An item with three criteria and a dispatch assigned two of them, plus briefs containing an empty subset, an omitted assigned criterion, and evidence mapped only to an omitted criterion.
red_test_sketch.when: The briefing skill validates or produces each brief.
red_test_sketch.expect: All malformed briefs are refused, while a brief containing both assigned criteria and mappings only to included criteria succeeds.

proposals.hole: The stale-facade check lacks boundary cases for versions exactly equal to, immediately below, and above the shipping version, including prerelease ordering.
proposals.proposed_ac: Facade-version checks use semantic version ordering: the exact shipping version and later compatible versions proceed, while the immediately preceding version and prereleases of the shipping version refuse with the required final version.

red_test_sketch.given: PATH binaries reporting the version immediately below the requirement, an associated prerelease, the exact requirement, and a later compatible version.
red_test_sketch.when: Each protected workflow performs its version check.
red_test_sketch.expect: The first two refuse naming the required version, and the exact and later versions proceed to the introduced verb.

proposals.hole: A malformed, empty, or nonzero `work --version` result is not covered and may be treated as current or leak an unrelated parser error.
proposals.proposed_ac: If the PATH facade's version command fails or returns an empty or unparsable version, the protected workflow refuses and names that it could not establish the required facade version.

red_test_sketch.given: PATH binaries whose version command exits nonzero, prints nothing, and prints non-version text.
red_test_sketch.when: The tracker attack path, panel render step, or poster checks the facade.
red_test_sketch.expect: Each workflow refuses before invoking a new verb and reports the version-detection failure and required version.

proposals.hole: Attestation validation can race with a change to the item's rendering or named spec between record validation and marker creation, allowing a marker to be written for a document that is no longer current.
proposals.proposed_ac: Attestation is serializable with changes to the attackable document: it either writes a marker for the current digest or refuses, and never reports success while leaving only a marker for a superseded document.

red_test_sketch.given: A valid record and an attestation operation paused after record validation but before marker creation.
red_test_sketch.when: The item's criteria, description, or named spec changes before attestation resumes.
red_test_sketch.expect: Attestation refuses or validates the new document; it does not report success by writing only the old digest.

proposals.hole: The attestation criterion compares the record with the tracker-born rendering file but does not explicitly require that file to equal a fresh facade rendering, so a stale committed file and matching stale record may attest after the item changes.
proposals.proposed_ac: A tracker-born item cannot be attested unless its attack document is byte-equal to a fresh `work acceptance render` result for the current item; a stale rendering file is refused without a marker.

red_test_sketch.given: A tracker-born item with a closed record matching its committed rendering file, followed by a criteria or description amendment that does not update that file.
red_test_sketch.when: The old record and file are passed to `work acceptance attacked`.
red_test_sketch.expect: Attestation refuses as stale and writes no marker; regenerating, re-attacking, and supplying the current rendering succeeds.

proposals.hole: A3 says a tree with no records is green but does not distinguish a genuinely empty tree from failure to enumerate an unreadable attack directory, so dependency failure can silently become success.
proposals.proposed_ac: Failure to enumerate any configured attack-record location makes the CI gate red and names the unreadable location; only successful enumeration finding zero records is green.

red_test_sketch.given: One temporary tree with no records and readable record locations, and another whose record location cannot be enumerated.
red_test_sketch.when: The whole-repo attack gate runs on each tree.
red_test_sketch.expect: The readable empty tree is green, while the enumeration failure is red and names the affected location.

proposals.hole: The gate is said to run over every record, but no criterion requires it to report all independently bad records rather than stopping after the first, leaving later open records undiscovered in the same run.
proposals.proposed_ac: A gate run with multiple invalid records is red and names every invalid record discovered in that run, regardless of traversal order.

red_test_sketch.given: A tree containing an unparseable record, an open record, and a stale record in different directories.
red_test_sketch.when: The whole-repo gate runs once.
red_test_sketch.expect: The result is red and identifies all three files and their respective failure classes.

proposals.hole: A12 says every child renders newly edited criterion text, but children may cite different criteria from the same spec; the boundary between a cited and an uncited edit is untested.

red_test_sketch.when: Only criterion A's text is edited.
red_test_sketch.expect: Only the A child's rendering changes, both prior attestations cease to cover their items, and neither child becomes claimable until the spec is re-attacked and they are re-attested.

proposals.hole: The criteria require the taxonomy to exist but never require an attack to walk every taxonomy row for every criterion or prevent closure when a row is neither resolved nor ruled out with a reason.
proposals.proposed_ac: For every criterion presented to the attack, the resulting record resolves or rules out with a reason each of inverse, empty or boundary, dependency failure, repeated or concurrent invocation, and idempotency; the record cannot close while any required row is absent or unexplained.

red_test_sketch.expect: The checker reports the missing taxonomy rows by criterion and refuses to close the record.
red_test_sketch.given: An attack record whose behavioural findings are dispositioned but whose criterion analysis omits one or more taxonomy rows or rules one out without a reason.
red_test_sketch.when: The attack checker evaluates the record.

proposals.hole: The rendering criteria do not require the item's description to appear in the rendered document, although the design makes that description part of every tracker-born attackable document and its digest.
proposals.proposed_ac: Rendering an item with a non-empty description emits that description before its rendered criteria, while rendering the same criteria after changing only the description changes the output and the tracker-born document digest.

red_test_sketch.expect: The first rendering contains the description before the criteria, and the second rendering and its digest differ from the first.
red_test_sketch.given: A tracker item with a non-empty description and unchanged non-empty criteria.
red_test_sketch.when: The item is rendered, its description is changed, and it is rendered again.

proposals.hole: Nothing requires render output to use the single `- **ID** text` bullet grammar promised to the downstream parsers, so arbitrary Markdown could satisfy the current content and byte-equality criteria.
proposals.proposed_ac: Each resolved or full-text criterion emitted by `work acceptance render` uses the `- **ID** text` bullet form accepted by spec-lint and the verdict poster, and the complete output parses successfully in both consumers without translation.

red_test_sketch.expect: Every criterion is emitted in the canonical bullet grammar, and both existing readers parse the render directly into the same ordered IDs and text.
red_test_sketch.given: An item containing multiple full-text and cited criteria.
red_test_sketch.when: The facade renders the item and the unmodified output is passed to spec-lint's and the verdict poster's criteria parsers.

proposals.hole: The prose says a cited entry with no text emits no criterion, but the criteria only test the case where the entire rendering becomes empty; they do not cover omission of an empty citation from a mixed, otherwise non-empty field.

red_test_sketch.when: `work acceptance render` renders the item.

proposals.hole: The seven required consumers do not all have a criterion requiring them to cite the standard: ACL-A7 is scoped to skills that write or amend criteria, while the attack and review-panel skills judge criteria, and ACL-A13 does not require either to cite the standard.

red_test_sketch.expect: All seven named skills contain a resolvable citation to the one deployed standard in the relevant clause, and a repository scan finds no private restatement in any of them.
red_test_sketch.given: The installed configuration for every supported tool after the standard-adoption slice.
red_test_sketch.when: The seven named deployed skills and the shared standard are inspected.

proposals.hole: The decision promises that the separate spec-quality standard cites this acceptance-criteria standard, but no criterion inspects that document; the slice list also omits this promised edit.

red_test_sketch.given: The deployed spec-quality standard after the standard-adoption slice.

proposals.hole: The new shared skill is promised to enter `src/` through the admission gate with an admission argument tied to the copies it removes, but no criterion requires a complete admission record or tests that the installer actually admits it.

red_test_sketch.given: The new shared skill and the source-tree edits that remove its predecessor copies.
red_test_sketch.when: The repository's admission and staging checks run.

proposals.hole: No criterion pins the classification rule that an item is spec-born only when every criterion is a citation; a mixed item could incorrectly use the spec and its record as its attackable document while still satisfying the rendering criteria.
proposals.proposed_ac: An item whose criteria are exclusively citations into its named spec is classified as spec-born and uses that spec and its adjacent record; an otherwise identical item with one full-text line is classified as tracker-born and uses `.work/attacks/<item-id>.md` and `.work/attacks/<item-id>-ac-attack.json`.

red_test_sketch.expect: The citation-only item selects the spec document and record, while the mixed item selects the two item-specific paths under `.work/attacks/`.
red_test_sketch.given: Two items naming the same spec, one containing only valid citations and the other containing those citations plus one full-text criterion.
red_test_sketch.when: The facade and tracker-item attack path determine each item's attackable document and record.

proposals.hole: ACL-A13 only checks that tracker-item workflow instructions are present; no criterion demonstrates that following the path actually renders, attacks, stores both files at the required paths, and attests the item.
proposals.proposed_ac: A real tracker-item attack-path invocation for a tracker-born item writes the current rendering to `.work/attacks/<item-id>.md`, writes the closed record to `.work/attacks/<item-id>-ac-attack.json`, and adds an attestation matching that rendering's digest only after the checker succeeds.

red_test_sketch.expect: Both files exist at the item-specific paths, the record closes against the rendering, and exactly one matching marker is present after successful checking.
red_test_sketch.given: An open tracker-born feature with non-empty criteria, no attack files, and no attestation.
red_test_sketch.when: An agent follows the deployed tracker-item attack path through completion.

proposals.hole: The attestation criteria do not cover the defined closing-revision rule for a record containing proposals that were all rejected; the only empty-acceptance case mentioned is a record with no proposals.
proposals.proposed_ac: A closed record with one or more proposals, all dispositioned as rejected and with no acceptance revisions, attests against its attacked revision when that revision equals the current attackable-document digest.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attestation succeeds and writes one marker carrying the attacked revision's digest.
red_test_sketch.given: A parseable closed record whose proposals are all rejected, whose acceptance list is empty, and whose attacked revision matches the current attackable document.
red_test_sketch.when: `work acceptance attacked ID --record PATH` is invoked.

dispositions.rationale: Rejected. A facade older than the claim gate cannot refuse on behalf of a gate it does not ship; the version check lives in the consumers that invoke the new verbs (ACL-D8), and the claim gate arrives with the facade version that ships it.

Rejected, recorded in the out-of-scope list: a claim, an attestation, a round emission or a post each hashes or compares at its own moment, and an amendment landing after that moment is caught by the next gate (ACL-D5, ACL-D6). Serializing two backend writes into one transaction is beyond the facade's boundary and buys nothing the digest binding does not already give.
Rejected as already true: the checker reads its lens registry live, so once the behavioural-outcome lens is registered no record lacking it closes; the deployed attack skill states this rule.
